text_blocks.snippet: U.S. citizens generally do not need a visa to visit Canada for stays under 180 days. For stays longer than 180 days, a visitor visa (also known as a Temporary Resident Visa) may be required. To apply, you'll need a valid passport and other supporting documents, and you may need to pay a processing fee.
snippet_highlighted_words: To apply, you'll need a valid passport and other supporting documents, and you may need to pay a processing fee

text_blocks.snippet: 1. Determine if you need a visa:

list.snippet: If you are a U.S. citizen and your visit is for less than 180 days, you likely do not need a visa.
If you are not a U.S. citizen, or your visit will be longer than 180 days, you will need to determine if you need a visa based on your citizenship and purpose of visit.
You can check specific requirements based on your nationality and situation on the Government of Canada website.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. If you need a visa, gather necessary documents:

list.snippet: Passport: Ensure your passport is valid for the duration of your stay.
Application Forms: Complete the required application forms (available on the Government of Canada website).
Photos: Provide passport-sized photos that meet specific requirements.
Proof of Funds: Demonstrate you have sufficient funds to support yourself during your stay.
Other Supporting Documents: This may include a detailed travel itinerary, invitation letter from friends or family, or other documents depending on your situation.
You can apply online or by mail, depending on your circumstances and the specific visa type.
If applying online, you'll need to create an account on the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website.
If applying by mail, you may need to submit your application to a Visa Application Centre (VAC).
You will need to pay the required application fee.
Processing times can vary, but you can expect it to take anywhere from a few weeks to a few months.
Ensure your application is complete to avoid delays.
If you have a valid U.S. visa, it may be helpful in your application, but it does not guarantee approval.
VFS Global is the authorized third-party service provider for Canadian visa applications in some locations, according to VFS Global.
If you are a U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder), you will need to provide your green card along with your passport.
